title: Principles of Family Development
description: Family development in society to include applications of social and behavioral science concepts, theory and research, behavioral patterns within families, social and cultural contexts, self-reflection, family dynamics, family transitions, resource management, marriage, parenting, divorce, and aging within families.

title: Child and Adolescent Development from a Cultural Perspective
description: Theories and research regarding child and adolescent development using a cultural and contextual approach with emphasis on understanding of diversity and cultural variation.
notes: Liberal studies premajors and majors and students seeking teaching credentials will complete

title: Human Development Across the Lifespan
description: Biological, cognitive, and socio-emotional development from conception to old age drawing on psychological and sociological theoretical perspectives and research to examine development within cultural contexts.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Principles of Observation: Child Development Laboratory
description: Multiple methods of observing and recording individual and group behavior of children. Observations required.

title: Child, Family, and Community Engagement
description: Individual and family needs and the social institutions and agencies attempting to meet these needs. Social issues, service programs, program analyses, and program effectiveness emphasized.

title: Learning Environments and Developmentally Appropriate Practices
description: Design, implementation, and evaluation of developmentally appropriate practices for children and families.

title: Foundations of Human Health, Nutrition, and Safety
description: Health, safety, nutrition practices and policies in the context of family, culture, and community.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See

title: Child and Family Community Services
description: Review and critical evaluation of community service agencies and social institutions serving children and families. Assessment of child and family needs, program effectiveness, evidence-based practice, and accessibility to diverse families.
notes: Not open to students with credit in CFD 272

title: Family Dynamics and Development
description: Theory and research on family dynamics and development from initial attraction to commitment and through all stages of the family. Family dynamics in couples, parent-child, and sibling relationships.
notes: Not open to students with credit in CFD 135

title: Developmentally Appropriate Practice for Children in Early Childhood Education and Family Contexts
description: Developmentally appropriate practice (DAP) for promoting child learning, development, and wellbeing within early childhood education, care, and family contexts. Design and evaluation of DAP activities based on research and best practices in the field.
notes: Not open to students with credit in CFD 275

title: Child Health, Nutrition, Safety, and Wellbeing
description: Practices and policies for promoting child health, safety, nutrition, and overall wellbeing within early childhood education, care, family, culture, and community contexts
notes: Not open to students with credit in CFD 278

title: Interactions in Culturally Diverse Families
description: Family interaction patterns throughout the life cycle in a multicultural society. Emphasis on theories, research findings, and family practices.

title: Parenting: Context, Research, and Application
description: Parenting and parent education in context to include attachment, discipline, parent-child interactions, parenting styles and practices. Professional applications for child health and well-being through parenting based on research and theory.

title: Research, Assessment, and Evaluation of Children and Families
description: Methods for measuring child, caregiver, and family behavior. Evaluation of reliability and validity. Includes research design, sampling techniques, data collection strategies, and values/ethics.

title: Human Development & Learning: Infancy to Toddlerhood
description: Physiological, psychological, cognitive, and socio-emotional development of the human organism in cultural contexts from conception to three years of age.

title: Human Development and Learning: Early to Middle Childhood
description: Physiological, psychological, cognitive, and socio-emotional development of the human organism in cultural contexts from age 3 to age 12.

title: Human Development and Learning: Adolescence to Adulthood
description: Physiological, psychological, cognitive, and socio-emotional development of the human organism in cultural contexts from age 12 to old age.

title: Building Leadership and Communication Skills in Human and Family Development Programs
description: Development of leadership, communication, conflict resolution, and supervision of professionals in human and family development programs, including child development programs.

title: Laboratory Experience: Infancy to Toddlerhood
description: Directed experiences in mainstream infancy and toddlerhood settings. Observing, screening, assessing, designing, and implementing developmentally appropriate activities.
notes: Negative TB test and Community Care Licensing clearance needed prior to the first day of class.

title: Laboratory Experience: Early Childhood
description: Directed experiences in mainstream early childhood settings for children ages 3 to 6 years old (e.g., preschool and kindergarten). Observing, screening, assessing, designing and implementing developmentally appropriate activities.
notes: Negative TB test and Community Care Licensing clearance needed prior to the first day of class

title: Laboratory Experience: Middle Childhood to Adolescence
description: Directed experiences in middle childhood to adolescence settings (e.g., elementary through secondary schools). Observing, screening, assessing, designing and implementing developmentally appropriate activities.
notes: Negative TB test and Community Care Licensing clearance needed prior to the first day of class

title: Laboratory Experience: Development Across the Lifespan
description: Directed experiences in settings across the lifespan. Observing, screening, assessing, designing and implementing developmentally appropriate interactions for children, families, caregivers, etc.
notes: Negative TB test and Community Care Licensing clearance needed prior to the first day of class

title: Observational Learning Experiences: Infants and Toddlers
description: Observations of infants and toddlers in various developmental contexts. Observation of screening, assessment, and developmentally appropriate activities.
notes: Not open to students with credit in CFD 378A. Three hours of laboratory (video observation) for each unit of credit (weekly)

title: Observational Learning Experiences: Preschool/ Kindergarten
description: Observations of young children of preschool through kindergarten ages in various developmental contexts. Observation, screening, assessment, and developmentally appropriate activities.
notes: Not open to students with credit in CFD 378B

title: Early Language and Literacy Development in a Linguistically Diverse Society
description: Language acquisition and early literacy development. Brain development and socio-emotional learning. Applications of developmentally appropriate and culturally responsive practice to enhance language, literacy, and school readiness.

title: The Hospitalized Child
description: Psychosocial needs of hospitalized child. Best practices for working with children and their families, and application of patient care vs. family centered care. Stress reduction, coping theories, and role of certified child life specialist.

title: Kumeyaay Shamull Project: Child and Family Development
description: Indigenous development and family patterns across the lifespan. Kumeyaay sustaining and revitalizing of cultural and socio-linguistic identity; theories of glocalization and multicultural development; socio-cultural, socio-linguistic, socio-emotional, and socio-political analysis of indigenous communities and relationship to dominant society
notes: This course includes a field placement experience component.

title: Violence in Relationships
description: Impact of relationship violence on individual development and ecological relationships. Historical and cultural contexts, child abuse and neglect, courtship violence, elder abuse, and violence in communities.

title: The Human-Nature Connection: Developmental Perspectives
description: Exploring effects of nature exposure on physical, emotional, and cognitive development. Emphasis on strategies for integrating contact with the natural environment into children’s lives and educational experiences. Examines nature-based therapeutic methods and their applications. Includes field experience in outdoor learning settings.

title: Promoting Behavior Support and Classroom Organization in Early Childhood Settings
description: Individual and systems-level approach to supporting young child behavior. Strategies for self-regulation, and three-tiers intervention, in early education settings and at home, to support all children, a targeted group of children who require additional support, and individual children who require intensive support.

title: Administration of Early Childhood Education Programs
description: Programs for young children: design, implementation, and evaluation. Research applications and legal requirements for public and private sectors.

title: Conﬂict Regulation and Resolution Across Relationships and Lifespan
description: Review and application of theories and research on conflict regulation, management and resolution across relationship contexts and across the lifespan. Observations of conflict and applications of conflict resolution to students’ lives.
notes: This course is not open to students with credit in CFD 578

title: Disability: Conception through Adolescence & Early Adulthood
description: Experiences of disabled individuals, conception to 25 years, and their families. Psychopathology, etiology, ableism, disabling environmental conditions, structural inequities, diagnostics, and educational systems. Observations of individuals with disabilities and their families with a focus on inclusion
notes: This course is not open to students with credit in CFD 590

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See

title: Field Experience in Child and Family Development Programs
description: Work experience in child and family development. Application of theoretical and evidence-based information with reflective supervision from faculty and field supervisor. Development of professional identity, cultural self-awareness, and career goals.
notes: 100 placement hours required. Negative TB test and Community Care Licensing clearance needed prior to the first day of class.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Divorce and Remarriage
description: Integration of family theories and research findings. Emphasis on adjustment to divorce and remarriage throughout life cycles, across cultures, social classes, and ethnicities.

title: Child Abuse and Family Violence
description: Multidisciplinary approach to child abuse and family violence including maltreatment, mistreatment, neglect, sexual abuse.

title: Family School Partnerships in Early Childhood Classrooms
description: Prepares future educators to develop strengths-based partnerships with diverse families. Emphasizes cultural humility, structural barriers, and home-to-school strategies for engagement. Grounded in ecological and culturally responsive frameworks to foster equity-centered family-school collaborations in early childhood classrooms.

title: Theories in Socio-Emotional Development
description: Socio-emotional development from infancy to adulthood. Theory and research regarding emotions, relationship-based development, cultural and societal contexts.

title: Public Policy and Professional Ethics in Child and Family Development
description: Ethical guidelines and other standards related to child and family development. Informed advocates for equitable educational practices and policies.

title: Professional Development and Mentorship in Human and Family Development Programs
description: Problem analysis and development of successful organizational strategies for child development program delivery. Leadership, effective communication, social and ethical issues from a multicultural perspective.

title: Conflict Resolution Across the Life Span
description: Theories of conflict development and resolution across lifespan. Parenting styles, discipline, behavior and class management, and conflict resolution techniques used in relationships. Directed experiences using conflict resolution techniques in various settings.
notes: Negative TB test and Community Care Licensing clearance needed prior to the first day of class

title: Observation and Assessment of Young Children’s Environments and Relationships
description: Ecobehavioral and developmental techniques and procedures to measure development, relationships, and environments. Emphasis on assessment use for educational planning and environmental improvements. Administration of measures in class and in field.

title: Family Involvement and Engagement with Young Children: Services and Resources
description: Role of parents and caregivers in supporting and enhancing developmental outcomes. Home visitation programs, practices, and techniques. Field experience to assist students in building the bridge between research and practice.

title: Disability: Conception through Emerging Adulthood
description: Experiences of disabled individuals, conception to 25 years, and their families. Psychopathology, etiology, ableism, disabling environmental conditions, structural inequities, diagnostics, and educational systems. Directed experience with individuals with disabilities and families, with a focus on inclusion.
notes: Three hours a week of field experience to be arranged. Negative TB test and Community Care Licensing clearance needed prior to the first day of class.

title: Early Childhood Mental Health: Theory and Practice
description: Neurorelational framework to understand brain development and mental health. Emotional and behavioral regulation support at home and in educational settings.

title: Advanced Studies in Child and Family Development
description: Advanced study of selected topics.
notes: See

title: Reflective Learning Portfolio
description: Capstone course to mentor child development majors to integrate knowledge acquired throughout child and family development program. Create portfolio and reflective essay.
notes: Major code: 08231.

title: Seminar in Family Processes
description: Analysis of selected research in family structure, development, and crisis.

title: Seminar in Family Therapy Theory and Techniques
description: Family therapy theory and techniques to include cognitive-behavioral, multigenerational, psychodynamic, strategic, and structural models. Epistemological, theoretical, and foundations of family systems theory.

title: Seminar in Counseling Theories and Techniques
description: Psychotherapy theory and techniques to include cognitive-behavioral, emotion-focused, family systems, person-centered, and psychoanalytic. Interpersonal neurobiological foundation of psychological development and its theoretical and epistemological constructs.

title: Seminar in Diverse Families
description: Critical examination of issues related to diverse families and various factors that impact children in diverse family contexts to include race, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, immigration status, ability, national origin, family formation, family structure, and pathways to parenthood.

title: Seminar in Professional Development and Professionalism
description: Growth and leadership in child and family development to include advocacy, career trajectories, professional identity, service, and strengths.

title: Seminar in Early Childhood Mental Health Career Development
description: Career development theories and techniques to include decision making models, interrelationships among and between family, work, and other life roles and factors; and multicultural issues in career development.

title: Seminar in Professional Law and Ethics in Counseling
description: Ethical standards, legal statutes, and regulations established by American Ethical standards, legal statutes, and regulations established by the American Counseling Association and the Board of Behavioral Sciences related to the practice of family therapy and psychotherapy. Child and elder abuse assessment and reporting, confidentiality, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, involuntary commitment, patients’ rights, privileged communication, other legal and ethical concerns specific to licensed professional clinical counselor profession.

title: Seminar in Human Development Theories- Attachment and Affect Regulation in Young Children
description: Advanced child and human growth theories. Attachment and affect regulation applications, models, research, and theories. Developmental crises, disability, and psychopathology.

title: Seminar in Human Development Theories- Intervention and Prevention Lifespan Approach
description: Advanced child and human growth and development theories. Intervention and prevention applications, models, research, and theories. Developmental crises, disability, and psychopathology.

title: Seminar in Supporting Early Childhood Mental Health
description: Psychotherapeutic theories and techniques for early childhood mental health specialists and practitioners to include positive behavior support models. Multidisciplinary models of response to crises and trauma using multicultural approach.

title: Neurorelational Framework for Early Childhood Mental Health Treatment
description: Early childhood mental health practices, processes, and theories in dyadic psychotherapy.

title: Early Childhood Intake Assessment, Diagnosis, and Treatment Planning
description: Assess, diagnose, and plan for treatment of young children and their families using a neurorelational framework.

title: Therapeutic Skills and Techniques for Early Childhood Mental Health
description: Clinical work preparation with young children and families. Evidenced- based programs and treatment modalities. Peer reflective supervision and feedback.

title: Play and Integrated Curriculum
description: The role of play in designing integrated curriculum for children birth to age 8. Emphasizes anti-bias education, developmentally appropriate practices, family partnership, emergent curriculum and creativity to optimize developmental outcomes.

title: Advanced Topics in Child and Family Development
description: Intensive study in specific areas of child and family development.
notes: See

title: Advanced Field Experiences A
description: Directed experience in early care and education settings for children 0-5. Screening, assessing, designing and implementing developmentally appropriate activities, supporting children with social-emotional and behavioral needs.
notes: The course is required in both fall and spring semesters.

title: Advanced Field Experiences B
description: Mental health and well-being of young children and families in culturally diverse communities. Multicultural theories and knowledge bases to clinical situations, strengths within diverse cultures, thoughts and feelings working with families from diverse cultures.

title: On-Site Coaching and Consultation in a Clinical Setting
description: Professional competence, self-awareness, and understanding through reflective practices. Increasing capacity to work effectively with families, infants, and young children.

title: Research Methods and Program Development
description: Research in child and family development: criteria and procedures for conducting research. Development of programs pertaining to children and families; literature review, proposal development, planning steps for implementation.

title: Advanced Clinical Experience and Group Supervision
description: Clinical field experience with individuals and groups. Advanced clinical supervision of group processes and working with young children and families experiencing trauma.

title: Seminar in Complexities of Child and Family Development
description: Complexities of child and family development (CFD), integration of material across CFD topic areas and across theory, research, observation, and assessment. Focus on developing professional presentation and writing that reflects integrating and analyzing information across CFD areas and identifying implications.
notes: Successful completion of the comprehensive exam is required for the graduation of Plan B students in addition to completion of this course.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a thesis or project for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university, also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.
